text.tspan: Level 1 — sensor to kernel
This is the layer that's entirely fixed silicon and kernel —
nothing here was ever patched this session. The /dev/videox
node is where userspace first gets access, but the raw data
sitting there is still unprocessed Bayer mosaic, not a viewable
image.
This is where nearly all of this session's early debugging lived —
the debayer shader fix (row 2) and the AWB/CCM tuning (row 1)
both live here, pinned to the iGPU via DRI_PRIME. By the
bottom row, the camera is a named, discoverable PipeWire
node (libcamera_input.__SB_.PC00.LNK0), ready for any
consumer.
This is the whole chain's actual bottleneck, isolated: the debayer
output is already DMA-BUF-backed, and it's libcamerasrc's
own caps template — not the driver, not PipeWire — that
discards that fact one step later.
Level 2 — libcamera and PipeWire
Level 3 — GStreamer capture and hardware encode
This is where the GSC/HuC saga lived — the coral rows only
work at all because of the i915 driver switch. The bottom row
is the fork point: RTP payload (rtpvp9pay) for a live network
stream, or matroskamux for a local file — both were tested
this session, RTP only for VP9 given the AV1 RTP gap.
Level 4 — transport back to decode and screen
That closes the full loop, sixteen stages total, sensor to screen.
The two GPU-hardware rows (coral, in levels 3 and 4) are the
only stages that differ by codec — this exact structure is what
we validated for VP9; for AV1, only the encode/decode boxes
themselves are proven, not the transport row connecting them
(the open item you just confirmed).
The only change between the two diagrams is that one box —
libcamerasrc's caps advertisement — and its downstream
consequence. Everything else in the chain (sensor, kernel,
debayer, vapostproc, encode) stays exactly as validated
throughout this whole session; the patch doesn't touch any
of that.
